first_impression.reaction: My fiancee wants a sand thing, so I searched it. The intro tells me what's on the page and gets out of the way, which I appreciate. I jumped to the FAQ and the legal section first, because that's the only bit where getting it wrong actually matters. The scripts themselves I skimmed. Not my department.

journey.quote: A sand ceremony is a symbolic ritual, so in Australia the legal words under sections 45 and 46 of the Marriage Act 1961 still have to be said around it.
journey.reaction: Right up top, with section numbers. That tells me someone checked the law instead of just writing nice words.

journey.quote: The pour sits well after the vows and rings, just before the pronouncement, or straight after the welcome.
journey.reaction: Which is it? 'Well after' and 'just before' in the same breath reads like a contradiction, and the takeaways line says the same odd thing. The body section is clearer. Small thing, but sloppy wording is where I start doubting the rest.

journey.quote: What matters is that the pour never sits inside the legal lines, which are said on their own, clearly, in front of your witnesses.
journey.reaction: Useful, practical rule. That's the actual takeaway for me.

journey.section: A sand ceremony and the legal words
journey.quote: As at November 2026, the form of ceremony sits in section 45 of the Marriage Act 1961, and the celebrant's explanation sits in section 46.
journey.reaction: Date, statute, section, links to the legislation. This is the standard I want from every planner site and rarely get.

journey.section: A sand ceremony and the legal words
journey.quote: If you marry overseas, the marriage must be valid under the law of the country where it happens, and valid under Australian law had it taken place here, to be recognised in Australia, so speak to a lawyer to confirm your certificate.
journey.reaction: Honest. You're telling me to get a lawyer rather than pretending you are one. Good.

journey.section: A sand ceremony at a beach or destination wedding
journey.quote: Before you settle on the setting, put these questions to the venue or, for a public beach, the local council.
journey.reaction: Questions I can actually ask, not 'we handle everything'. Practical.

journey.quote: Wedded Concierge brings the venue, travel and vendors together in one plan, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: 'Anywhere in the world' is a big claim with nothing behind it, and this pitch lands in the middle of a how-to before I've seen any proof. It's the one line on the page that sounds like marketing.

journey.section: A sand ceremony at a beach or destination wedding (CTA)
journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, your Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel and vendors with you as a single point of contact, working in your time zone.
journey.reaction: Fine, it's concrete. But 'vendors' is exactly where I ask: do you take a cut from the venue or the celebrant? Page doesn't say.

journey.section: Planning the ceremony around the pour
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: 'In writing before you commit' is the right phrase. Still doesn't tell me what the fee is or whether there are commissions, so I'm not clicking yet.

unanswered_questions: Do you take a commission or mark-up from venues, celebrants or other suppliers?
What does the Wedded Advisor fee cover, and how is it charged?
How do you choose or vet the celebrants and vendors you'd put us in front of?
Show me a real wedding you've planned, with the actual budget.

turn_offs_found.quote: Wedded Concierge brings the venue, travel and vendors together in one plan, anywhere in the world.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported scope claim, and a sales line before the page has shown any evidence (the legal section comes later).

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the scripts and the beach checklist
Our celebrant, for the fill-in template

cta_reaction.quote: Start the conversation with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: I came for a script, not a planner, and the closing CTA comes after real evidence, which I respect. But I won't enquire with anyone until I know the fee model and whether there are supplier commissions. I'd bookmark the site because the legal section was properly done.

top_3_changes: Fix the contradictory placement wording in the FAQ. Old: "The pour sits well after the vows and rings, just before the pronouncement, or straight after the welcome." New: "The pour usually sits after the vows and rings, just before the pronouncement, or straight after the welcome."

Match the Key takeaways line to the body. Old: "The pour sits well after the vows and rings and before the pronouncement, and your celebrant sets the final order." New: "The pour usually sits after the vows and rings and before the pronouncement, and your celebrant sets the final order."

Drop the unsupported scope claim in the mid-article CTA. Old: "brings the venue, travel and vendors together in one plan, anywhere in the world." New: "brings the venue, travel and vendors together in one plan."

checks.check: Every point has an exact quote from the draft
No invented brand facts; missing info listed in unanswered_questions
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Suggested edits stay within deferred limits (no fee, commission, sourcing or vetting copy added) and use exact old/new strings

open_questions.question: Daniel's core objection (commissions, fee model, how celebrants and vendors are sourced and vetted) is deferred by the brand. Log it for a future fee-model page rather than treat it as a must-fix for this post?

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'sand ceremony script' on behalf of his fiancee; low personal relevance for Daniel is expected for a ritual how-to.
